explanation: A time-valid Office parent launched a scripting shell. Legitimate automation can produce this behavior. PowerShell command line contains an encoded-command indicator; this is context for investigation, not proof of malicious activity. A scripting process was associated with a public remote TCP endpoint snapshot. Public addressing is not malicious by itself; connection direction is unknown. An Office-launched encoded shell and a public TCP observation share the same verified process generation within 60 seconds. This observed chain does not confirm C2.
limitations: Risk score is a triage heuristic, not malware probability.
TCP snapshot polling may miss short-lived sockets; a row does not establish connection direction.
Registry notifications do not identify the writer PID.
